title: PCM Leadership Training
content:
PCM Leadership Training

Understand different people. Lead with more choice.

A practical 16-hour Process Communication Model® programme for leaders who want to understand what motivates different people, recognise stress earlier and adapt communication to real people and real situations.

16 hours·Personal Leadership Profile·In person ET·EN·RU Book a 20-minute introduction call

Leadership through PCM

Different people need different ways of being led.

PCM gives leaders a practical framework for understanding personality differences, psychological needs, motivation and behaviour under stress.

It also starts with the leader: understanding your own strengths, preferred ways of leading, reactions under stress and patterns you may not notice as quickly in yourself.

The goal is not to learn one “correct” leadership style, but to recognise what is happening — in yourself and in others — and choose a way of communicating that fits the person and the situation.

What participants learn

From understanding people to leading them more consciously

Recognise people faster

Notice communication clues, personality preferences and the first signs that contact is becoming more difficult.

Motivate more precisely

Understand different psychological needs and choose ways of communicating that support motivation and engagement.

Return communication to a constructive track

Recognise early stress and misunderstanding, adapt your approach and reduce the risk of escalation.

Understand yourself as a leader

See your own strengths, preferred leadership patterns, stress responses and ways to stay more effective in difficult situations.

Your Leadership Profile

Your own communication is part of the leadership system.

Before the training, each participant completes the official PCM questionnaire and receives a personal Leadership Profile. It connects the model directly to your own communication, motivation, interaction preferences and patterns under stress.

Personality Structure & strengthsCommunication & interaction preferencesPsychological needs & motivationStress patterns & practical reflection

How the training works

Learn it. Notice it. Try it in real life.

01

Profile

Start with your personal PCM Leadership Profile.

02

Understand

Build a shared language for personality, motivation and stress.

03

Practise

Work individually, in pairs and in groups with practical exercises and cases.

04

Apply

Use the time between sessions to notice patterns in everyday work and try new approaches in real situations.

05

Follow up

Meet again after the training to discuss what happened in practice, ask questions and refine how PCM is used in everyday work.

The goal is not to finish the training and leave the profile on a shelf. Follow-up helps turn PCM into an everyday working tool.

For schools & education

A teacher is a leader, too.

PCM Leadership Training can be used in schools for teachers and school leaders, without turning it into a separate “school version” of the model.

A teacher leads every day: creates a frame, guides learning, motivates, keeps a group together and adapts communication to different people and situations.

PCM gives schools a shared language for understanding what motivates different students, how they take in information, how stress changes behaviour and communication, and what can help restore contact.

For experienced teachers, much of this may already happen intuitively. PCM helps make that knowledge more conscious, easier to discuss and easier to use consistently across a school team.

Format

16 hours with time to apply what you learn

4 × 4 hoursFour meetings with space between them for real-life observation and practice. In personFor organisations, teams and schools. ET · EN · RUThe training can be delivered in Estonian, English or Russian. Practical by designTheory, individual work, pair/group exercises, video analysis and real group cases.

What changes after the training

More options in the moments that matter

Clearer communication

More choice in how you explain, direct, give feedback and build trust with different people.

Earlier recognition of stress

Notice when communication starts to move off track and respond before tension grows.

More conscious motivation

Understand what different people need in order to stay engaged, resourceful and able to contribute.
